title: Appendix A — Proposal
text:
a title > Analysis of Premier League data
team member names > We are Chris Frantz, Jack Freimann, and Joey Burica.
a short description of the project > We will be examining data on players and teams in the English Premier League to make some conclusions based on our research questions.
2-3 broad research questions the team is interested in exploring > How are Premier League players distance covered affected by weather? Is there a significant home field advantage? What is more important: more goals scored or less goals conceded?
the reasons/inspirations behind choosing the topic > We are all soccer players that frequently watch the Premier League, so Premier League data is perfect for us.
one potential data set that can be used to answer the research questions > Stathead/FBref
communication plan, ie, primary communication channel (eg, Google Chat, Slack, Email), expected response time (eg, 24 hours during the week), meeting time (eg, “we will meet 7-8pm every Wednesday”) > We all have each others’ contact information. We will expect responses within 1 day. We will meet every Wednesday at 7 pm.
roles–everyone is expected to contribute to the project but having leads helps with accountability. In particular, determine (1) point of contact–the main person to email the instructor/preceptors, (2) technical lead–the person who will oversee the code base and website, (3) style lead–the person who will make sure the code is following the COMP/STAT 112/212: Code Styling Guide > Jack will be the main point of contact, Chris will be the technical lead, and Joey will be the style lead.
conflict resolution, ie, if a team member misses a deadline, how will the team handle it? How will you make decisions if the team is split 50/50 on a something? > We will attempt to do things as a team so that we are all accountable. We have 3 so a tiebreak will be available.
a rough implementation plan, ie, list of tasks with due date and roles–refer to the list of deliverables when building your list. The plan should be added as GitHub Issues within the project repository–see the callout box below for details. > The first thing that we need to do is find a good data source. That is in the works as you are reading this. The next thing we need to do after reviewing the data is hone in on one of the specific research questions listed above. After that we will be able to complete our project with multiple, detailed, visualisations that help address the question of interest. Please let me know if there is anything you think we also need to do. Signing off, the contact guy.

title: Appendix B — Case Study
text:
Our case study is: How News Media Covers Trump and Clinton: An analysis of images in news media by The Pudding. https://pudding.cool/2018/01/chyrons/
Instructions: record your observations about its data story structure, ie, how the report unfolds the story. The analysis should be added to appx/case-study.qmd file. Make sure to cite the referenced resources.
They start by laying some background information. It gives information necessary to understanding the visual, as well as describing the question/interesting unknown that the article will answer.
In the text, they tell a story about one aspect of the topic, and give a visualization that help to explain that aspect. Each visualization is explained and connected to the text. Examples are given to help the user understand.
The visuals they use are somewhat interactive, moving the mouse shows a different part of the visual, and the user can experiment and learn at their pace. The text scrolls by but the the interactive visual remains, allowing the story itself to be interactive.
They end the article by summarizing their analysis in a brief paragraph. They restate what should be taken from the article and what can be done by the reader to avoid some of the problems mentioned.
Further specificity about data collection and analysis is added at the very end, in smaller font, to be accesible but not integral to the article.
